questions.prompt: In an unquoted service path like C:\Program Files\My App\service.exe, why does the missing quotation mark matter?
options: It doesn't — Windows always resolves the correct path regardless
Windows tries each space-delimited segment as a potential executable in turn, and an attacker who can write to an earlier segment's path can hijack execution
It only matters for services running as a standard user account
It causes the service to fail to start entirely
questions.explanation: Windows attempts C:\Program.exe, then C:\Program Files\My.exe, before the real path — writable access to any earlier segment lets an attacker's binary run instead, often as SYSTEM.

questions.prompt: What do the "Potato" family exploits (JuicyPotato, RoguePotato, etc.) actually abuse?
options: A buffer overflow in the Windows kernel
Coercing a privileged local service holding SeImpersonatePrivilege into authenticating to an attacker-controlled listener, then capturing that token
A weakness in NTLM password hashing
questions.explanation: Potato-family exploits coerce a service with SeImpersonatePrivilege into authenticating locally to an attacker listener, then reuse the captured token — no exploit of a memory vulnerability required.

questions.prompt: Why is there no single 'privilege escalated' event to alert on for token-impersonation-based escalation specifically?
options: Windows doesn't log privilege escalation at all
The token was already legitimately available to the service — it was just used somewhere it shouldn't have been, not stolen through an alertable event
These attacks always disable event logging first
Token impersonation only works on domain controllers
questions.explanation: The privilege wasn't stolen through a distinct malicious act — it was legitimately available via SeImpersonatePrivilege and simply directed somewhere unintended, leaving no dedicated escalation event.

questions.prompt: Why does the lesson connect local privilege escalation to the earlier Discovery and LOLBin lessons?
options: They're entirely unrelated topics placed together by coincidence
Attackers rarely bother enumerating a domain from an account with no local administrative rights — escalation often precedes and enables that activity
Discovery commands are only possible after privilege escalation succeeds
LOLBins require SYSTEM privileges to execute at all
questions.explanation: Local privilege escalation is frequently the step that makes the subsequent Discovery and LOLBin activity worthwhile — an attacker with only low-privilege access has much less reason to enumerate broadly.
